X.note: The sepia terrain with bathymetry contours and the low-poly gantry cranes and ship have a nice stylized look. The icons overlap each other, so two documents, two cranes and a ship merge into one clump. The location is never named, so there is no place label. The Korean coast is only implied. The date badge '1971–74' reads well. The caption 'LORE: one columnist's account, not a record' is cryptic. The source line is small and low-contrast on phone. Most of the right half is empty gray sea.

Y.note: A clean, tilted satellite-style map. Minnesota is highlighted against its dimmed neighbours with clear borders, and a callout pins Minneapolis. The callout text is large and high-contrast. The caption is readable. The source line is small and long. The imagery is slightly muddy and desaturated, and the pin is tiny. The state-level view is generic and has no data visual, but the place is obvious at once.

why: Y tells you where and what in a glance with clean, readable labels, while X's icons pile into a muddled cluster with no location label despite its more stylized art.
top_fix_for_weaker: Space the crane, ship and document icons apart and scale them up, then add a clear location label (e.g. 'Ulsan, South Korea') with a country-context inset. Replace the cryptic 'LORE:' caption with a plain sentence, and enlarge the source line and give it more contrast.
